memory.content: Every CLI run uses </dev/null, a timeout and an __EXIT=$? marker, logs to /tmp/<cli>-<label>-<date>.log, and runs detached with nohup.
If a CLI hits its usage limit, stop and tell the owner: don't switch models and don't pay.
When the owner names CLI + model + effort, use exactly that; never silently switch CLI or model.
Every CLI example or report names the terminal, the model and the effort level.
The owner is consulted on every task; only the orchestrator talks to the owner, CLIs report to the orchestrator.
Merge only with the owner's explicit OK and green CI.
No deploy without an explicit order from the owner, and back up the production database before deploying.
Every implementation PR is reviewed by a strong model (default: grok CLI, grok-4.7, xhigh) before merge, and all findings of every severity are fixed.
Reviewers run read-only; executors write only in the task's branch or worktree; one writer per branch at a time.
Never use models that train on data with the owner's code or data; verify no-training/no-retention before using a free model.
Never print, copy or pass into prompts CLI auth files, tokens or keys; logins are done by the account owner.
Never run git config --global; set commit authorship only via GIT_AUTHOR_* and GIT_COMMITTER_* env vars. Never force push or rebase published branches.
kiro-cli --effort only applies on the v2 engine (default, no --v3); v3 drops the effort.
Exit code 0 is not proof a CLI did the work: check stopReason/denied_actions/is_error in the output and git status/git log.
GitHub operations (branch, commit, push, PR, merge) are delegated to a catalog implementer CLI with exact commands and written prohibitions, never Claude CLI; the orchestrator verifies afterwards.
Done means lint, typecheck, tests and build all exit 0; UI changes also need screenshots in light and dark themes (and mobile when the screen changes).
Keep Docker/containers off except during a visual proof; turn them off right after.
Skills changed during work should also be copied to the owner's chosen skills backup folder, if one is configured.
Owner secrets, account numbers and real financial or personal data never go into a repository; real data is used only locally in a test database and deleted afterwards.

skills.content:
---
name: cli-agy
description: >-
  Use when a request says to run the Google Antigravity CLI (agy) on the box
  (gemini-3.8/3.7/3.6-flash, gemini-3.1-pro, claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5,
  gpt-oss-120b) to review (read-only) or execute a task (write).
---
# cli-agy

Binary: `agy` (Google Antigravity CLI), Google account login. `agy models` lists models and doubles as login check (exit 1 "Please sign in" = logged out).

## Models and effort
- Ids carry the level: `gemini-3.8|3.7|3.6-flash-{low,medium,high}`, `gemini-3.1-pro-{low,high}`, `claude-opus-5-5-{low,medium,high}`, `claude-sonnet-5-5-{low,medium,high}`, `gpt-oss-120b-medium`.
- Use `--model <id-with-level>`, or `--model <base> --effort <level>`. Rejected (exit 1, before spending): base without effort, id+conflicting effort, nonexistent level. **No xhigh or max anywhere**; for those use another CLI.
- Without `--model` it uses an unreported account default: always pass `--model`.

## Base command (cwd = workspace; cd first)
```bash
cd "$REPO" && agy -p "$(cat /tmp/<label>-prompt.md)" --model gemini-3.8-flash-high --output-format json <MODE> < /dev/null
```
- JSON: `conversation_id`, `status`, `response`, `usage`, `denied_actions`. `stream-json` is best for logs.
- `--print-timeout 30m` returns partial output with SUCCESS/exit 0 when hit (only clue: "[agy] print timeout" in stderr).

## Permission modes
Global rules in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` (keep; deny beats everything, even skip-permissions):
```json
{"permissions":{"allow":["command(git diff)","command(git log)","command(git show)","command(git status)","command(rg)","command(ls)"],
 "deny":["write_file(/tmp/agy-rev/)","command(git push --force)","command(git push -f)","command(git push --force-with-lease)","command(git reset --hard)","command(git config --global)"]}}
```
| Role | MODE |
|---|---|
| Reviewer | no flag, run **inside a worktree under `/tmp/agy-rev/<label>`** (file writes denied there; only allow-listed simple commands run) |
| Executor | `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (only way to run shell in `-p`; deny rules still apply) |
- **Outside `/tmp/agy-rev` the default mode is NOT read-only**: no flag, `--mode plan` and `--mode accept-edits` all write files. Never run a reviewer directly in the repo.
- Compound commands (`&&`, `|`, `;`) are denied even if each part is allowed: tell reviewers one command per call.
```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/agy-rev && git -C "$REPO" worktree add --detach /tmp/agy-rev/<label> <sha>
cd /tmp/agy-rev/<label> && agy -p "..." --model <id> --output-format json < /dev/null
git -C "$REPO" worktree remove --force /tmp/agy-rev/<label>
```

## Detached, sessions, resume
```bash
cd "$REPO"; LOG=/tmp/agy-<label>-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log; export PROMPT_FILE=/tmp/<label>-prompt.md
nohup bash -c 'timeout 3h agy -p "$(cat "$PROMPT_FILE")" --model gemini-3.8-flash-high --dangerously-skip-permissions --output-format stream-json; echo "__EXIT=$?"' > "$LOG" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
```
- Resume: `agy -p "continue: ..." --conversation <id> --model <id> <MODE>` (repeat model and mode). `-c` picks the latest from **any** folder: always use `--conversation`.

## Pitfalls
- **A denied command wipes the response**: empty `response`, SUCCESS, exit 0, `denied_actions` set, "no output produced". Always check `denied_actions`.
- Each minimal call costs ~12k input tokens. Lost login: pass the Google URL to the requester; the account owner logs in.

## Never
skip-permissions on a reviewer; a reviewer outside `/tmp/agy-rev/`; loosening the deny rules (`write_file(*)`/`command(*)`); `git config --global`; merge/deploy/force push/PR without order; touching or printing the oauth token file.

## Examples
Review (agy, claude-opus-5-5-high, read-only worktree):
```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/agy-rev && git -C "$REPO" worktree add --detach /tmp/agy-rev/rev-x HEAD
cd /tmp/agy-rev/rev-x && agy -p "$(cat /tmp/rev-x-prompt.md)" --model claude-opus-5-5-high --output-format json < /dev/null > /tmp/agy-rev-x.log 2>&1
git -C "$REPO" worktree remove --force /tmp/agy-rev/rev-x
```
Worker (agy, gemini-3.8-flash-high, write):
```bash
cd "$REPO" && agy -p "$(cat /tmp/task-x-prompt.md)" --model gemini-3.8-flash-high --dangerously-skip-permissions --output-format stream-json < /dev/null > /tmp/agy-task-x.log 2>&1
```

---
name: cli-claude
description: >-
  Use when a request says to run the Claude Code CLI (claude) on the box with
  opus, sonnet, fable or haiku and effort low to max, to review (read-only) or
  execute a task (write).
---
# cli-claude

Binary: `claude` (Anthropic Claude Code), claude.ai login. Check `claude auth status`, but a real one-line test is the truth: an expired OAuth session can still report `loggedIn: true` and fail with `is_error:true`, exit 1. If login is down, don't run it; tell the requester (the account owner logs in). cli-router lists Claude alternatives, used only with an order to switch.

## Models and effort
`--model opus|sonnet|fable|haiku` or full name; `--effort low|medium|high|xhigh|max`. `--fallback-model` (only `-p`).

## Base command
```bash
cd "$REPO" && claude -p "$(cat /tmp/<label>-prompt.md)" --model opus --effort high --output-format json <MODE> < /dev/null
```
`-p` skips the folder-trust dialog: only known repos. `--max-budget-usd` caps spend.

## Permission modes (`--permission-mode`)
| Role | MODE |
|---|---|
| Reviewer | `--permission-mode plan` |
| Reviewer running tests | `--permission-mode dontAsk --allowedTools "Read Grep Glob Bash(git diff*) Bash(git log*) Bash(npm test*)"` |
| Executor | `--permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools "Bash(npm *) Bash(git add*) Bash(git commit*)"` |
| Extra lock | `--disallowedTools "Bash(git push*) Bash(git merge*)"` |

## Detached, resume
```bash
cd "$REPO"; LOG=/tmp/claude-<label>-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log; export PROMPT_FILE=/tmp/<label>-prompt.md
nohup bash -c 'timeout 3h claude -p "$(cat "$PROMPT_FILE")" --model opus --effort high --output-format json --permission-mode plan; echo "__EXIT=$?"' > "$LOG" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
```
Check `is_error`/`result`. Session: `session_id`; resume `-r <id>` or `-c`. Prefer nohup over its own `--bg` so logs match other CLIs. Never use `--bare` (needs an API key).

## Never
`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions`, `bypassPermissions` (settings may skip the warning, so this is absolute); `git config --global`; merge/deploy/force push/PR/`ultrareview`/`--cloud` without order; logging in on your own. Claude CLI never does GitHub operations in the workflow.

## Examples
Review (claude, opus, high, read-only):
```bash
cd "$REPO" && claude -p "Review only diff <base>..HEAD against: <task>. Edit nothing. Findings critical/important/minor, or clean." \
  --model opus --effort high --permission-mode plan --output-format json < /dev/null > /tmp/claude-rev-x.log 2>&1
```
Worker (claude, opus, medium, write without push):
```bash
cd "$REPO" && claude -p "$(cat /tmp/task-x-prompt.md)" --model opus --effort medium --permission-mode acceptEdits \
  --allowedTools "Bash(npm *) Bash(git add*) Bash(git commit*)" --disallowedTools "Bash(git push*)" --output-format json < /dev/null > /tmp/claude-task-x.log 2>&1
```

skills.description: Use when a request says to run the Command Code CLI (cmdc) on the box with models like deepseek-v4.1-flash, kimi-k3, glm-5.3, qwen3.8-max, claude-opus-5-5 or xai/grok-4.7, to review (read-only) or execute a task (write).
skills.content:
---
name: cli-cmdc
description: >-
  Use when a request says to run the Command Code CLI (cmdc) on the box with
  models like deepseek-v4.1-flash, kimi-k3, glm-5.3, qwen3.8-max,
  claude-opus-5-5 or xai/grok-4.7, to review (read-only) or execute a task
  (write).
---
# cli-cmdc

Wrapper: `~/.local/bin/cmdc` (Command Code). Login check: `cmdc status`.

## Setup not to touch
- Command Code needs Node 22+, but the machine's main node is different. A private node 22 lives in `~/.local/node22` and `cmdc` is a wrapper using it. Always call `cmdc` (`cmd`/`command-code` use the main node and fail). Never replace the main node.
- After `npm i -g command-code@latest`, recreate the wrapper (npm overwrites it):
  `printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec "$HOME/.local/node22/bin/node" "$HOME/.local/lib/node_modules/command-code/dist/index.mjs" "$@"\n' > ~/.local/bin/cmdc && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/cmdc`

## Models and effort
Live list: `cmdc --list-models`. E.g. `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`, `kimi-k3`, `glm-5.3`, `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, `qwen3.8-max`, `minimax-m3`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gemini-3.8-flash`, `xai/grok-4.7`. `--effort` depends on model; `max` works on `deepseek-v4.1-flash` (first line confirms "Reasoning effort set to max").

## Base command (cd into the repo)
```bash
cd "$REPO" && cmdc -p "$(cat /tmp/<label>-prompt.md)" -m deepseek-v4.1-flash --effort max \
  --skip-onboarding --no-auto-update -t <MODE> < /dev/null
```
`-t` trusts the project. `--output-format json`/`--verbose` for logs. `--max-turns` default 100; overflow exits 8.

## Permission modes
| Role | MODE |
|---|---|
| Reviewer (default) | `--yolo` + deny rules in `.commandcode/settings.local.json` (below). Runs tests/`git diff`; writes, commit and `>` are blocked. Restore the settings file afterwards. |
| Reviewer without shell | none or `--plan`: read/grep/glob only; any shell (even `ls`) blocked |
| Executor | `--yolo` (the only way to write/run shell in `-p`) |

Reviewer deny file (never commit it; save and restore any original):
`{"permissions":{"deny":["Write","Edit","Write(*)","Edit(*)","Shell(git commit*)","Shell(git push*)","Shell(git reset*)","Shell(rm *)","Shell(*>*)"]}}`
`Shell(*>*)` also blocks `2>&1`. Executor locks: e.g. `{"permissions":{"ask":["Shell(git push:*)"],"deny":["Shell(git push --force*)","Shell(git reset --hard*)"]}}` (`deny` always blocks; `ask` blocks in `-p`).

## Detached, finish, resume
```bash
cd "$REPO"; LOG=/tmp/cmdc-<label>-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log; export PROMPT_FILE=/tmp/<label>-prompt.md
nohup bash -c 'timeout 3h cmdc -p "$(cat "$PROMPT_FILE")" -m deepseek-v4.1-flash --effort max --skip-onboarding --no-auto-update -t --yolo --verbose; echo "__EXIT=$?"' > "$LOG" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
```
Sessions: `~/.commandcode/projects/<cwd-dashed>/<id>.jsonl`. Resume: `--session <id-prefix>`, `-r <id|name>` or `-c`; name runs with `-n "<label>"`.

## Pitfalls
Exit is always 0: look for "requires permissions"/"Blocked by permission deny rule"/"BLOCKED" and check `git status`. Lost login: `cmdc login` needs the account owner.

## Never
`--yolo` on a reviewer without the deny file; `git config --global`; merge/deploy/force push/PR without order; `--cloud` without order.

## Examples
Review (cmdc, deepseek-v4.1-flash, max, read-only, no shell):
```bash
cd "$REPO" && cmdc -p "Review only diff <base>..HEAD against: <task>. Edit nothing. Findings critical/important/minor, or clean." \
  -m deepseek-v4.1-flash --effort max --skip-onboarding --no-auto-update -t < /dev/null > /tmp/cmdc-rev-x.log 2>&1
```
Worker (cmdc, deepseek-v4.1-flash, max, write):
```bash
cd "$REPO" && cmdc -p "$(cat /tmp/task-x-prompt.md)" -m deepseek-v4.1-flash --effort max \
  --skip-onboarding --no-auto-update -t --yolo -n "task-x" --verbose < /dev/null > /tmp/cmdc-task-x.log 2>&1
```

skills.content:
---
name: cli-codex
description: >-
  Use when a request says to run the OpenAI Codex CLI (codex) on the box with
  gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-luna or the gpt-5.6 line, to review
  (read-only) or execute a task (write).
---
# cli-codex

Binary: `codex` (OpenAI). Login: ChatGPT account (`codex login status`).

## Models and effort
| Model (`-m`) | Listed efforts | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `gpt-6.1-sol` | low..max, ultra | mapping/arena/review (high), judge (xhigh) |
| `gpt-6-astra` | low..max, ultra | judge (medium) |
| `gpt-6-luna` | low..max | implementation (max) |
| `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-sol/terra/luna` | low..max(, ultra) | — |
- Live catalog: `codex debug models` (`supported_reasoning_levels`). Use only listed efforts: an unlisted one may be silently accepted (unknown behavior). Invalid effort = 400, exit 1.
- The config may set a default effort: always pass `-m` and `-c model_reasoning_effort=...`.

## Base command
```bash
codex exec -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=high -C "$REPO" <MODE> \
  -o /tmp/<label>-final.md "$(cat /tmp/<label>-prompt.md)" < /dev/null
```
`-o` saves the last message; `--json` emits JSONL; `--skip-git-repo-check` outside git.

## Sandbox modes (`-s`)
| Role | MODE |
|---|---|
| Reviewer | `-s read-only` (writes fail "Read-only file system") |
| Executor, no commit | `-s workspace-write` (`.git` is read-only) |
| Executor with commit | `-s workspace-write --add-dir "$REPO/.git"` |
| + push / npm install | above + `-c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true` (untested) |

## Detached, finish, resume
```bash
export REPO=/path PROMPT_FILE=/tmp/<label>-prompt.md
LOG=/tmp/codex-<label>-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log; export FINAL="${LOG%.log}-final.md"
nohup bash -c 'timeout 3h codex exec -m gpt-6-luna -c model_reasoning_effort=max -C "$REPO" -s workspace-write --add-dir "$REPO/.git" -o "$FINAL" "$(cat "$PROMPT_FILE")" < /dev/null; echo "__EXIT=$?"' > "$LOG" 2>&1 &
```
- Session id: `session id:` line at top. Resume: `codex exec resume <id> "continue: ..."` (or `--last`), repeating `-m`, effort, `-s`. Don't use `--ephemeral` if you may resume.

## Pitfalls
- Without `< /dev/null` it may wait on stdin. "Reading additional input from stdin..." is harmless.
- It auto-loads `~/.codex/skills` and can get distracted: for short tasks say "do not load skills" and verify files/git log.
- Sandbox denials exit 0; the error is only in the response / `aggregated_output`. Verify results.
- No deny list: the reviewer lock is `read-only`.

## Never
`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` or `-s danger-full-access` without order; `git config --global`; merge/deploy/force push/PR without order; `codex cloud` without order.

## Examples
Review (codex, gpt-6.1-sol, high, read-only):
```bash
codex exec -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=high -C "$REPO" -s read-only \
  -o /tmp/codex-rev-x-final.md "Review only diff <base>..HEAD against: <task>. Edit nothing. Findings critical/important/minor, or clean." < /dev/null > /tmp/codex-rev-x.log 2>&1
```
Worker (codex, gpt-6-luna, max, commit, no push):
```bash
codex exec -m gpt-6-luna -c model_reasoning_effort=max -C "$REPO" -s workspace-write --add-dir "$REPO/.git" \
  -o /tmp/codex-task-x-final.md "$(cat /tmp/task-x-prompt.md)" < /dev/null > /tmp/codex-task-x.log 2>&1
```

---
name: cli-devin
description: >-
  Use when a request says to run the Devin CLI (devin, Cognition) on the box
  with models like swe-2, claude-opus-5-5-<effort>, gpt-6-sol-<effort>,
  deepseek-v4.1-flash or kimi-k3, to review (read-only) or execute a task
  (write).
---
# cli-devin

Binary: `devin` (Cognition). Login check: `devin auth status`.

## Models and effort
- Live list: `devin models list`. **Effort is part of the model id**; there is no `--effort` flag.
- Ids: `swe-2-medium|high|max`, `swe-1-7-lightning-medium`, `claude-opus-5-5-low|medium|high|xhigh|max`, `claude-fable-5-1-<effort>`, `gpt-6-sol-<effort>`, `gpt-6-luna-<effort>`, `kimi-k3-low|high|max`.
- Bare families (`claude-opus-5.5`, `grok-4.7`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `glm-5.3`, `gemini-3.8-flash`...) use the default effort; use the full id for a specific effort.

## Base command (cd into the repo)
```bash
cd "$REPO" && devin -p "$(cat /tmp/<label>-prompt.md)" \
  --model claude-opus-5-5-high --respect-workspace-trust false <MODE> < /dev/null
```
- `--respect-workspace-trust false` is required in `-p` for untrusted folders. `--export /tmp/<label>-conv.md` saves the conversation each turn (progress log).

## Permission modes
| Role | MODE |
|---|---|
| Reviewer | `--permission-mode auto` (default): read tools only; others rejected ("rejected a tool call that requires confirmation") |
| Executor | `--permission-mode dangerous`: approves everything; the only mode that wrote in `-p` |
`accept-edits` was not enough in tests. With `dangerous` the only lock is the prompt: write the prohibitions there, and use it only in the task's repo/worktree.

## Detached, finish, resume
```bash
cd "$REPO"; LOG=/tmp/devin-<label>-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log
export PROMPT_FILE=/tmp/<label>-prompt.md EXPORT="${LOG%.log}-conv.md"
nohup bash -c 'timeout 3h devin -p "$(cat "$PROMPT_FILE")" --model claude-opus-5-5-high --respect-workspace-trust false --permission-mode dangerous --export "$EXPORT"; echo "__EXIT=$?"' > "$LOG" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
```
- Session id: `devin list` in the repo (`-p` doesn't print it). Resume: `devin -r <id> -p "continue: ..." <MODE>` or `-c`. `--model` on resume switches models.

## Pitfalls
Without `dangerous` the executor exits 0 having done nothing; rejected writes show only in stderr. Check `git status`. `--cloud`/`devin cloud` run off the box: only with order.

## Never
`git config --global`; merge/deploy/force push/PR without order; `dangerous` on a reviewer.

## Examples
Review (devin, claude-opus-5-5-high, read-only):
```bash
cd "$REPO" && devin -p "Review only diff <base>..HEAD against: <task>. Edit nothing. Findings critical/important/minor, or clean." \
  --model claude-opus-5-5-high --respect-workspace-trust false --permission-mode auto < /dev/null > /tmp/devin-rev-x.log 2>&1
```
Worker (devin, swe-2-high, write):
```bash
cd "$REPO" && devin -p "$(cat /tmp/task-x-prompt.md)" --model swe-2-high --respect-workspace-trust false \
  --permission-mode dangerous --export /tmp/devin-task-x-conv.md < /dev/null > /tmp/devin-task-x.log 2>&1
```

# cli-droid

Binary: `droid` (Factory AI). Live model list: `droid exec --help`.

## Models and effort (`-m`, `-r`)
| Model | Efforts | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `claude-opus-5-5` | low..max | medium |
| `claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-fable-5.1` | off..max | high |
| `gpt-6-sol` (CLI default), `gpt-6-astra` | low..max | medium |
| `gpt-5.6-sol/terra/luna` | none..max | medium |
| `grok-4.7`, `grok-4.6` | low..xhigh | high |
| `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `gemini-3.8-flash` | low..high | high |
| `kimi-k3`, `glm-5.3`, `qwen3.8-max`, `claude-haiku-5-5` | see --help | — |
Always pass `-m` and `-r`.

## Base command
```bash
droid exec -m claude-opus-5-5 -r high --cwd "$REPO" -o json -f /tmp/<label>-prompt.md <MODE> < /dev/null
```
`-o json` ends with a line holding `result`, `session_id`, usage.

## Permission modes
| Role | MODE | Allows |
|---|---|---|
| Reviewer | none | Read files, git status/log/diff, ls, find |
| Executor, no push | `--auto medium` | Edit, install, build, test, commit; blocks push |
| Executor with push | `--auto high` | Above + `git push` |

## Detached, finish, resume
```bash
export REPO=/path/to/repo
LOG=/tmp/droid-<label>-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log
nohup bash -c 'timeout 3h droid exec -m claude-opus-5-5 -r high --auto medium --cwd "$REPO" -o json -f /tmp/<label>-prompt.md; echo "__EXIT=$?"' > "$LOG" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
```
- Log stays empty until the end; liveness = mtime of `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-dashed>/<session_id>.jsonl`.
- Resume: `droid exec -s <session_id> -m ... -r ... <MODE> "prompt"` (prompt required); `--fork <id>` branches. `droid search "<text>"`.

## Pitfalls
- Effort `max` hung twice with no output, also on resume. Use high/xhigh; if a max run stalls, kill and rerun in high in a new session.
- No `--auto` = every write fails. Unauthorized write compounds fail loudly (`is_error:true`, "insufficient permission", exit 1) — the only CLI that does.
- **Policy refusal**: with `GIT_AUTHOR_*` inside the shell command the model may refuse ("won't override git identity") and report success. Export the vars before calling droid.
- `--mission` spawns many workers; only with explicit order.

## Never
`--skip-permissions-unsafe`; `git config --global`; merge/deploy/force push without order, even in `--auto high` (say it in the prompt).

## Examples
Review (droid, claude-opus-5-5, high, read-only):
```bash
droid exec -m claude-opus-5-5 -r high --cwd "$REPO" -o json -f /tmp/rev-x-prompt.md < /dev/null > /tmp/droid-rev-x.log 2>&1
```
Worker (droid, claude-opus-5-5, high, write without push):
```bash
droid exec -m claude-opus-5-5 -r high --auto medium --cwd "$REPO" -o json -f /tmp/task-x-prompt.md < /dev/null > /tmp/droid-task-x.log 2>&1
```

skills.description: Use when a request says to run the xAI Grok Build CLI (grok) on the box with grok-4.7, grok-4.7-build-fast, grok-4.6 or grok-4.5, to review (read-only) or execute a task (write).
skills.content:
---
name: cli-grok
description: >-
  Use when a request says to run the xAI Grok Build CLI (grok) on the box with
  grok-4.7, grok-4.7-build-fast, grok-4.6 or grok-4.5, to review (read-only) or
  execute a task (write).
---
# cli-grok

Binary: `~/.grok/bin/grok`. Login via grok.com; `grok models` shows login and models.

## Models and effort
`grok-4.7` (server default), `grok-4.7-build-fast`, `grok-4.6`, `grok-4.5`. Effort `low|medium|high|xhigh` on 4.7/4.6; 4.5 up to high. The config may pin another default: always pass `-m` and `--effort`. Usage shows `grok-4.7-build` = same model.

## Base command
```bash
grok --no-auto-update -p "$(cat /tmp/<label>-prompt.md)" -m grok-4.7 --effort medium \
  --output-format json --cwd "$REPO" <MODE> < /dev/null
```
JSON returns `text`, `stopReason`, `sessionId`, usage; `streaming-json` for live logs.

## Permission modes
| Role | MODE |
|---|---|
| Reviewer | `--always-approve --deny Edit --deny Write --deny 'Bash(git commit*)' --deny 'Bash(git push*)' --deny 'Bash(git reset*)' --deny 'Bash(rm *)'` |
| Reviewer running tests | above + `--allow 'Bash(npm test*)'` |
| Executor | `--always-approve` (add `--deny 'Bash(git push --force*)'` etc. for hard locks) |
| Executor, file writes only | `--allow 'Write(*)' --allow 'Edit(*)'` |

## Detached, finish, resume
```bash
export REPO=/path/to/repo
LOG=/tmp/grok-<label>-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log
setsid nohup bash -c 'timeout 3h grok --no-auto-update -p "$(cat /tmp/<label>-prompt.md)" -m grok-4.7 --effort medium --always-approve --output-format json --cwd "$REPO"; echo "__EXIT=$?"' > "$LOG" 2>&1 < /dev/null & disown
```
- `__EXIT=` 0 ok, 1 error, 130/143 interrupted. Session: `sessionId`; `grok sessions list`.
- Resume: `grok --no-auto-update -p "continue: ..." -r <sessionId> -m grok-4.7 --effort medium --cwd "$REPO" <MODE>`. Repeat the write mode; it isn't inherited. Files already written stay.

## Pitfalls
- **Compound commands cancelled in `-p`** without `--always-approve` (even read-only `;`, `&&`, `|`): `stopReason: cancelled`, exit 0, no work. Use `--always-approve` + `--deny` (deny wins) and check `stopReason`.
- **Silent write refusal**: without `--always-approve`/`--allow Write(*)` it says "creating files", exits 0, writes nothing. Check `git status`.
- `xhigh` is much slower; fine for judge and heavy review.

## Never
`git config --global`; merge/deploy/force push/PR without order (say it in the prompt); `grok login` on your own (`grok login --device-auth` needs the account owner).

## Examples
Review (grok, grok-4.7, xhigh, read-only):
```bash
grok --no-auto-update -p "$(cat /tmp/rev-x-prompt.md)" -m grok-4.7 --effort xhigh \
  --always-approve --deny Edit --deny Write --deny 'Bash(git commit*)' --deny 'Bash(git push*)' --deny 'Bash(git reset*)' --deny 'Bash(rm *)' \
  --output-format json --cwd "$REPO" < /dev/null > /tmp/grok-rev-x.log 2>&1
```
Prompt: "Review only the diff <base>..HEAD against the task below. Edit nothing. Return findings as critical, important, minor (file:line and reason), or 'clean'."

Worker (grok, grok-4.7, medium, write):
```bash
grok --no-auto-update -p "$(cat /tmp/task-x-prompt.md)" -m grok-4.7 --effort medium \
  --always-approve --output-format json --cwd "$REPO" < /dev/null > /tmp/grok-task-x.log 2>&1
```
Prompt: "On branch <branch>, implement <task>. Run <tests>. Commit with GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* = <author>. No push, PR, merge or rebase. Reply with sha, what changed, test count."

  --effort is used), to review (read-only) or execute a task (write).
---
# cli-kiro

Binary: `kiro-cli` (Kiro/AWS), Builder ID login (`kiro-cli whoami`). `q`/`qchat` are legacy aliases.

## Models and effort
- Live list: `kiro-cli chat --v3 --list-models`: `claude-opus-5.5` (2.0x credits), `claude-sonnet-5.5`, `claude-opus-5`, `gpt-5.6-sol` (4.4x), `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-5.6-luna` (0.6x), `claude-haiku-4.5`, `deepseek-3.2`, `glm-5`, `auto` (default)...
- `--effort low..max` per model. **Effort only applies on the v2 engine (default, no `--v3`)**; v3 drops it. Without effort you may use `--v3`.
- Credits differ per model: use the requested one, not the priciest.

## Base command (no `--cwd`; cd first)
```bash
cd "$REPO" && kiro-cli chat --model claude-opus-5.5 --effort xhigh --no-interactive <MODE> \
  "$(cat /tmp/<label>-prompt.md)" < /dev/null 2> /tmp/kiro-<label>.err
```
Stderr is noisy `[INFO]`; keep it separate. `--output-format stream-json` for live logs.

## Permission modes
| Role | MODE |
|---|---|
| Reviewer | `--trust-tools=fs_read` (reads files only; no shell at all, not even git diff — put the diff in the prompt or a file) |
| No tools | `--trust-tools=` |
| Executor | `-a` (trust all) |
No deny list by flag.

## Detached, sessions, resume
```bash
cd "$REPO"; LOG=/tmp/kiro-<label>-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log
export PROMPT_FILE=/tmp/<label>-prompt.md ERR="${LOG%.log}.err"
nohup bash -c 'timeout 3h kiro-cli chat --model claude-opus-5.5 --effort medium --no-interactive -a "$(cat "$PROMPT_FILE")" 2> "$ERR"; echo "__EXIT=$?"' > "$LOG" < /dev/null &
```
- v2 session: newest `~/.kiro/sessions/cli/<uuid>.json`; check `session_state.rts_model_state.model_info.model_id` and `...additional_fields.overrides.output_config.effort` (absent = medium).
- v3 session: newest `~/.kiro/sessions/*/sess_*/session.json` (`modelId`, `effortLevel`). Report the session id.
- List: `kiro-cli chat --v3 --list-sessions -f json`. Resume: `--resume-id sess_<id>` or `-r`.

## Pitfalls
Without `-a` the executor writes nothing and exits 0. Denials show `[denied]` / `status: Failed` with exit 0.

## Never
`git config --global`; merge/deploy/force push/PR without order (`-a` frees everything — say it in the prompt); `--cloud` without order.

## Examples
Judge/review (kiro-cli v2, claude-opus-5.5, xhigh, read-only):
```bash
cd "$REPO" && kiro-cli chat --model claude-opus-5.5 --effort xhigh --no-interactive --trust-tools=fs_read \
  "$(cat /tmp/judge-prompt.md)" < /dev/null > /tmp/kiro-judge.log 2> /tmp/kiro-judge.err
```
Worker (kiro-cli v2, claude-sonnet-5.5, medium, write):
```bash
cd "$REPO" && kiro-cli chat --model claude-sonnet-5.5 --effort medium --no-interactive -a \
  "$(cat /tmp/task-x-prompt.md)" < /dev/null > /tmp/kiro-task-x.log 2> /tmp/kiro-task-x.err
```

# cli-opencode

Binary: `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` (install: `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash`; update `opencode upgrade`). Not on PATH: `export PATH=$HOME/.opencode/bin:$PATH`.

**Default: free models only, no key, no billing.** Optional free alternative; never replaces a default.

## Free models (`-m opencode/<id>`; live list `opencode models opencode`, they can disappear)
| Use | Models |
|---|---|
| **Default: no retention, no training** | `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` (first choice), `glm-5.3-flash-free`, `longcat-2.5-preview-free`, `space-bunny-free` |
| **Train on data: never with the owner's code or data** | `big-pickle`, `exo-free`, `mimo-v2.6-flash-free`, `mimo-v2.5-free`, `ll-alpha-free`, `nemotron-3-ultra-free`, `nemotron-3.5-lightning-free`, `nemotron-3.5-super-vl-free` |
`beam-free` retains data 30 days: avoid. Re-verify the no-training status before use. Effort: `--variant <low|high|max>` (free models may ignore it).

## Base command
```bash
export PATH=$HOME/.opencode/bin:$PATH OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1 OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE=1
cd "$REPO" && timeout 2h opencode run -m opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free --variant max "$(cat /tmp/<label>-prompt.md)" < /dev/null > /tmp/opencode-<label>.log 2>&1; echo "__EXIT=$?" >> /tmp/opencode-<label>.log
```
- **`< /dev/null` is mandatory**: without it `run` hangs silently.
- `--print-logs --log-level INFO` shows session id and `modelID=` (confirm the model). `--format json` for raw events. `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE=1` stops it reading `.claude/`.

## Permission modes (inline JSON in `OPENCODE_PERMISSION`)
| Role | How |
|---|---|
| Reviewer | `OPENCODE_PERMISSION='{"edit":"deny","bash":{"*":"deny","git diff*":"allow","git log*":"allow","git status*":"allow","git show*":"allow"},"webfetch":"deny"}'`, no `--auto` |
| Executor | `--auto` + `OPENCODE_PERMISSION='{"bash":{"git push*":"deny","gh *":"deny","git commit*":"deny"}}'` |
Denials show `✗ <cmd> failed` + "a rule which prevents you", exit 0: check `git status`. `--auto` approves everything not denied; executor only, always with the deny list. The orchestrator does git itself.

## Sessions
`opencode session list`, `opencode export <id>`, resume `opencode run -c "..." </dev/null` or `-s <id>`, `--fork`. Spend: `opencode stats`.

## Paid Zen/Go (only with explicit owner order)
`opencode auth login` (interactive) with a key from opencode.ai; Zen = pay per use (`opencode/<id>`), Go = subscription (`opencode-go/<id>`). `*-contributor` models train on data.

## Never
Training models with owner code/data; paid model, login or key without order; printing/copying `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`; `git config --global`, commit, merge, deploy, push, PR, `opencode github`/`opencode pr` without order.

## Example
Worker (opencode, opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free, max, write, no commit): base command above with `--auto` and the executor `OPENCODE_PERMISSION`.

skills.description: Use in the first conversation with a new owner, to introduce the bot, check and install AI coding CLIs, and set up the way of working.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use in the first conversation with a new owner, to introduce the bot, check
  and install AI coding CLIs, and set up the way of working.
---
# getting-started

**Always speak in the new owner's language** (detect it from their first message; this template is written in English only for portability). Short messages, one block at a time. Question cards one at a time; wait for the answer before the next. Every CLI example always names terminal + model + effort.

## 1. Intro
"I'm a hands-on code tech lead. I take a task (bug, screen, PR review), split it into steps and put the AI coding CLIs on this computer to work (grok, codex, droid, kiro, devin, cmdc, agy, opencode). At the end I show you the result with a PR, tests and proof it works. Merge and deploy only with your OK."

## 2. pstack
"I work with pstack, an engineering skill pack: understand the code before touching it, remove before adding, prove it works, write without fluff. It has skills to map, plan, test and review."

## 3. workflow-architect (one paragraph per stage)
"For bigger changes I use architect, adapted for CLIs. Each stage has a default model and you can swap any.
**Mapping.** One CLI reads the code without changing anything and writes how the affected part works today, where it's called, and what can break. E.g. grok, grok-4.7, xhigh.
**Arena.** Two CLIs from different model families get the same map and each designs a solution, isolated. E.g. droid, claude-opus-5-5, high vs codex, gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh.
**Judge.** A third CLI compares both proposals against the code, scores them, picks the base and says what to graft from the other. E.g. kiro-cli, claude-opus-5.5, xhigh.
**Spec and plan.** The decision becomes a spec and a plan of small tasks, tests first. It can stop here if you only want the design.
**Implementation.** A CLI writes the code following the plan on a separate branch. E.g. cmdc, deepseek-v4.1-flash, max.
**Review.** Another CLI reads the diff read-only and flags problems; they get fixed and re-reviewed. E.g. grok, grok-4.7, xhigh.
**PR and proof.** I run the tests, show proof it works and open the PR. Merge only the way you define."

## 4. Not mandatory
"None of this is mandatory. Small things I do directly, and you can skip architect anytime."

## 5. Calling a CLI
"When you want a specific CLI, say terminal, model and effort, e.g. 'run codex with gpt-6.1-sol on xhigh to review this diff', 'use kiro-cli with claude-opus-5.5 on xhigh to judge', 'implement with cmdc with deepseek-v4.1-flash on max'. I run exactly that, no switching; if the combo doesn't exist I tell you. Everything goes to a log you can follow."

## 6. Check and install
- Run the cli-router health check and show: installed+logged in, installed without login, not found.
- multiSelect card with allowCustom: "which do you want to install now?", one option per CLI that has a `cli-*` skill but is missing (max 6; others can be typed), plus "none for now".
- Install the chosen ones. Login belongs to the owner: hand over the screen for their step.
- A typed CLI outside the list: research how it installs, logs in and runs headless; test it; create a `cli-<name>` skill and add it to cli-router.

## 7. Setup cards
1. Way of working: "full architect on big changes" / "you write and review alone, no CLIs" / "ask me each task".
2. Models (only models that run on installed CLIs; each preset stage with terminal + model + effort): "economy" (free opencode and flash models) / "balanced" (strong only in mapping, judging, reviewing) / "maximum" (strongest everywhere) / "choose stage by stage" / "skip for now". Before the card explain: mapping, judging and reviewing need a strong model on high or xhigh because mistakes there are expensive; the arena uses two models from different families on high; implementation does well with a mid or fast model at max effort, since the spec decides almost everything.
3. Repository: "connect GitHub and pick the repo" / "start without a repo".
4. Safety: "merge and deploy only with my OK" (primary) / "merge on my behalf with green CI".

## 8. Close
Save the answers as memory, and adjust the defaults tables in workflow-architect and cli-router to the CLIs present. Then ask in plain text, no card: "ready. what do you want to do now?"

---
name: Grok Build harness
description: >-
  Use when a task should run through the Grok Build CLI on this box's terminal
  (grok-4.7, effort medium by default), always showing the work.
---
# Grok Build harness

Run tasks through the Grok Build CLI (`grok`) on this box's terminal. Don't substitute another model, skip the CLI, use the owner's computer, or hand the work to a cloud agent.

## When
Every time a task should go through grok (from the owner or an orchestrator). Always this box's terminal.

## Visibility
Show the work as it happens: what you run, model/effort, and the result. Don't hide commands, progress or outcomes.

## Defaults
- Binary `grok` (usually `~/.grok/bin/grok`), model `grok-4.7` (`-m grok-4.7`), effort `medium` unless the request says otherwise (terminal + model + effort are always explicit).
- Auth via `grok login` (grok.com). If it fails, run `grok login --device-auth` and hand the box to the owner. Never ask for a pasted key.

## Headless run
Read-only (grok, grok-4.7, medium):
```bash
grok --no-auto-update -p "$PROMPT" -m grok-4.7 --effort medium --always-approve --deny Edit --deny Write --deny 'Bash(git commit*)' --deny 'Bash(git push*)' --deny 'Bash(git reset*)' --deny 'Bash(rm *)' --output-format json --cwd "$WORKDIR" < /dev/null
```
Read-only without `--always-approve` is a trap: in `-p` compound commands needing approval are cancelled (`stopReason: cancelled`, exit 0, almost no work). Use `--always-approve` + `--deny` (deny wins). Check `stopReason`.

Agentic work (grok, grok-4.7, medium, write):
```bash
grok --no-auto-update -p "$PROMPT" -m grok-4.7 --effort medium --always-approve --output-format json --cwd "$WORKDIR" < /dev/null
```
Long jobs: background with timeout + `__EXIT` marker (see cli-router), `streaming-json` for progress, and surface meaningful beats.

## Prompt
Full task: goal, constraints, files/paths, definition of done. The CLI starts blank.

## After
Read the result and deliver the outcome: what ran and what came back. Don't dump raw logs unless asked.

skills.name: workflow-architect
skills.description: Use when the owner asks for architect, or wants to choose or change the model for each stage of a plan-and-implement flow (mapping, arena, judge, implementation, review, GitHub).
skills.content:
---
name: workflow-architect
description: >-
  Use when the owner asks for architect, or wants to choose or change the model
  for each stage of a plan-and-implement flow (mapping, arena, judge,
  implementation, review, GitHub).
---
# workflow-architect

The pstack architect flow run with the box's CLIs, one chosen model per stage. The request brings topic, repo and definition of done; this workflow doesn't pick the product or invent scope. Base recipe: pstack's `architect` skill (read-only; find with `find / -path '*pstack*/skills/architect/references' 2>/dev/null`). Exact commands: cli-router and each `cli-<name>`.

## 1. Start rule
- Show the owner the stage table (section 2: stage, CLI, model, effort) **once**, in a question card with "Confirm" and an option to swap a stage. Then don't ask again until the plan ends; mid-flow model doubts are settled by section 4.
- If a model fails (quota, login, nonexistent combo), use the listed backup and report it; with no backup, stop the stage and tell the owner. Usage limit hit: stop, don't switch or pay.
- Only the orchestrator talks to the owner; CLIs report to it.

## 2. Defaults (adjust to installed CLIs)
| Stage | CLI | Model, effort | Mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mapping | grok | `grok-4.7` xhigh | read-only |
| Arena A | droid | `claude-opus-5-5` high | read-only |
| Arena B | codex | `gpt-6.1-sol` xhigh | read-only |
| Arena alt | grok | `grok-4.7` xhigh | read-only |
| Judge | kiro-cli v2 | `claude-opus-5.5` xhigh | read-only |
| Implementation | cmdc | `deepseek-v4.1-flash` max, `--yolo` only in the task worktree | write |
| Review | grok | `grok-4.7` xhigh (`--always-approve` + `--deny`) | read-only; 3rd round may fix |
| GitHub ops | the task's implementer | same | write |
- Implementation backups: `glm-5.3-flash` max (cheap), `claude-sonnet-5.5` high (UI-heavy).
- Every implementation PR is reviewed by a strong model (default grok, grok-4.7, xhigh) before merge.
- Review fixes findings of **every** severity (critical, important, minor, real nit) in at most two rounds back to the implementer; if the 3rd review still finds issues, the reviewer fixes them in write mode, runs tests and build, and closes.
- GitHub (branch, commit, push, PR, merge): a catalog implementer (never Claude CLI) with exact commands and written prohibitions (no force push, no rebase of published branches, no amend, no `git config`, no merge/deploy out of order). Orchestrator verifies (`git ls-remote`, `gh pr view`).
- Merge only with the owner's OK and green CI. Never deploy without explicit order (back up the database first).

## 3. Catalog
- **Mapping/arena/review:** grok `grok-4.7` xhigh; codex `gpt-6.1-sol` high; droid `claude-opus-5-5` high; kiro-cli v2 `claude-opus-5.5` high/xhigh; devin `claude-opus-5-5-high|xhigh`; claude `opus` high/xhigh; agy `claude-opus-5-5-high` (max high); the orchestrator itself; opencode free models only if asked.
- **Judge:** kiro-cli v2 `claude-opus-5.5` xhigh; devin `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh`/`claude-fable-5-1-medium`; codex `gpt-6.1-sol` xhigh or `gpt-6-astra` medium; droid `claude-opus-5-5` xhigh or `kimi-k3` max; claude `opus` xhigh; grok `grok-4.7` xhigh.
- **Implementation/GitHub:** `deepseek-v4.1-flash` max (cmdc, droid, devin); `glm-5.3-flash` max (cmdc `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, droid, devin); `gpt-6-luna` max (codex, droid, devin); `claude-haiku-5-5` max (droid, devin, cmdc); `swe-2-max` (devin); sonnet 5.5 high; `gemini-3.8-flash-high` (agy); opencode `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` (`--auto` + deny, optional). Claude CLI never does GitHub ops.

## 4. Choosing
- **Strong, high effort** where design is decided or checked: mapping, arena, judge, review. A mapping error contaminates everything.
- **Mid/fast at max effort** where it's execution: implementation and GitHub follow a closed design and exact commands.
- Arena with **different families**; reviewer from a different family than the implementer; judge different from at least one candidate. agy has no xhigh/max.

## 5. Steps
Open a todo list, one entry per phase. Every CLI call follows cli-router (prompt file, nohup, `</dev/null`, timeout, `__EXIT`, log) and reports command, model, effort, log, session, result.
1. **Grounding.** Read-only mapping on current `origin/main` → `grounding.md`: request quoted, current flow with `file:line`, what couldn't be confirmed. Spot-check design-critical claims.
2. **Isolated arena.** Work dir `/tmp/arena-<topic>/` with `runner-prompt.md`, `design-red-flags.md`, `rationale-template.md` from architect's `references/` plus `grounding.md`. Each candidate in its own session, blind to the other, returns a package per the rationale template. Demand two structurally different designs.
3. **Cross judge.** Gets both packages, grounding and red flags; scores, picks the base, says what to graft and why. Verify its claims against the code.
4. **Synthesis.** Orchestrator writes `docs/superpowers/specs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<topic>-design.md`; candidates, grounding and verdict go in `docs/superpowers/specs/<topic>/`, committed on the task branch.
5. **Implementation** in the branch worktree against the design. Independent tasks may use `inherit` subagents (one writer per file), or parallel implementers in separate worktrees/branches merged and checked at the end. Deviations go back to the orchestrator. Done only with lint, typecheck, tests and build all exit 0. Repeated friction = architect Scrap phase: redo grounding and arena.
6. **Visual proof (UI).** Screenshots in light and dark themes, and mobile when the screen changes. Containers only during the proof, off right after.
7. **Review** (section 2 rules). A finding contradicting the approved design drops, with the reason.
8. **PR.** Implementer opens it with exact commands; orchestrator shows it to the owner. Merge only on OK + green CI. Deploy only on order.
Always: author only via `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*`; never `git config --global`; never force push; one writer per branch.

## 6. Changing
When the owner changes a default or adds/removes a model or CLI, update sections 2 and 3. A one-flow swap from the start card doesn't change the skill. A new CLI needs a `cli-<name>` skill registered in cli-router.

# workflow-grok

Orchestrate a written plan one task at a time. Plan, repo, branch and definition of done come from the request; this workflow doesn't pick the product or invent tasks.

No PR, merge or deploy mid-plan. Only when the whole plan is clean, and only if the owner already authorized going to merge. Otherwise stop at the end and show the state.

## Who talks to the owner
The orchestrator (this bot) coordinates and is the only one updating the owner: which task, what it does, and when commit and review closed. Workers report only to the orchestrator; say so in their prompt. Don't relay their chatter.

## Roles
- Execution: grok CLI, `grok-4.7`, effort medium (write mode, see cli-grok). Subagents inside the task are fine.
- Review: kiro-cli, `claude-opus-5.5`, effort medium, read-only (`--trust-tools=fs_read`, diff passed in the prompt; v2 engine to honor effort, see cli-kiro). Verify the session file and report the session id.
- Fix of findings: grok CLI, `grok-4.7`, effort high, only the finding's diff, not the next task.

## The loop
1. Read the task. Send one task. One writer per branch. Don't start the next until this review is clean.
2. Give the executor the exact scope, the tests the plan asks for, and what not to touch. It commits and pushes (no PR). It returns sha, changes, test count.
3. Send that diff to the reviewer: review what the task promised, not a tour of the repo. Findings as critical, important, minor, or clean. Don't ask it to propose the next task.
4. Any critical, important or minor: fix with grok-4.7 high; re-review only that diff. Repeat until clean.
5. Next task. At the end, follow the merge rule above.

## Judging findings
Check each finding against the plan before sending it for a fix. If the plan required it and the reviewer called it scope creep, the finding drops; tell the reviewer why. Real findings get fixed now; never push important or minor to a later task.

## Prompts
Each prompt carries the goal, paths, definition of done and what is out of scope. Workers start without this chat's history.
